memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Make a courtyard for the tabernacle. The south side shall be a hundred cubits long and is to have curtains of finely twisted linen, with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases and with silver hooks and bands on the posts. The north side shall also be a hundred cubits long and is to have curtains, with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases and with silver hooks and bands on the posts." - Exodus 27:9-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Around the tabernacle God places a courtyard, enclosed with linen curtains hung on posts. It marked a boundary — this space is set apart, this ground is holy. Anyone approaching would know exactly where the ordinary camp ended and God's dwelling began.

Boundaries are not unloving. In fact, this boundary made nearness possible. Without a marked space, there could be no ordered approach to a holy God; there would only be confusion or presumption. The curtain wall said both things at once: this is set apart, and there is a way in. Limits and welcome stood together.

We sometimes struggle with this. Our culture tends to treat all boundaries as restrictions on freedom, and we can carry that instinct into our faith, resenting anything God marks off as holy. But God's boundaries have always served relationship rather than blocked it. He sets things apart so that they can be treated rightly, and He sets us apart too — called to be holy, belonging distinctly to Him (1 Pet 1:15-16). The line God draws around your life is not a wall against you. It is the shape of belonging to Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I view God's boundaries as restrictions or as the shape of belonging to Him?
What has God set apart in my life that I have been treating casually?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, the boundaries You draw are not walls against me but the shape of belonging to You. Help me honour what You have set apart and live as one who is Yours. Amen.
